'''Orang Kanaq''' is one of the [[Malayic languages]], grouped under the [[Austronesian languages]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Austronesian Language Family|url=https://www.sorosoro.org/en/austronesian-languages/|website=Sorosoro|language=en}}</ref> It is spoken by the Orang Kanaq, one of the 19 [[Orang Asli]] groups in Peninsular Malaysia. The language is believed to have been extinct since the 1950s according to the [[UNESCO]] ''[[Atlas of the World's Languages in Danger]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlas of the world's languages in danger|url=https://unesdoc.unesco.org/ark:/48223/pf0000187026|website=[[UNESCO]]|page=209|date=2010|access-date=2024-12-14|author1=Christopher Moseley|author2=Alexandre Nicolas}}</ref>

A variant of [[Malay language|Malay]], Orang Kanaq is distinct from the dialects spoken by ethnic [[Malays (ethnic group)|Malays]] living near them.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Collins |first=James T. |date=1989 |title=Malay Dialect Research in Malysia [sic]: The Issue of Perspective |journal=Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde |language=en |volume=145 |issue=2/3 |pages=235–264 |doi=10.1163/22134379-90003253 |jstor=27864031 |doi-access=free}}</ref> All members of the Orang Kanaq tribe understand the language; however, its lexicon has been largely influenced by the Malay language.<ref name="psasir" />
